sub_answers.sub_question: Which mill closures, layoffs, or plant mothballings did the firm announce during industry downturns and on what dates?
sub_answers.text: International Paper established a pulp paper mill in 1937 and closed that paper mill in 1979 [d115837s2p0]. International Paper maintained wood products and container-producing facilities after 1979 but sold the wood products plant during 2006–2007 [d115837s2p0]. After the sale, Georgia Pacific closed the plywood mill it had purchased from International Paper (date of Georgia Pacific closure not specified beyond the sale period) [d115837s2p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which parliamentary hearings, inspector-general reviews, city council motions, organized rallies, or labor strikes specifically targeted the company’s announced restructuring plans, and what records or minutes document those actions?

What environmental impact assessments, human-rights or labor-rights reports, community impact statements, shareholder or NGO critiques, or local economic analyses criticized the company’s consolidation strategy and approach to downsizing?

Did any lawsuits, class actions, administrative enforcement proceedings, regulatory investigations, or monetary penalties arise from the company’s plant closures, layoffs, divestments, or fire-sale asset transfers, and what agencies or courts handled those cases?
sub_answers.text: The Attorney General of the District of Columbia brought suit in an attempt to prevent Ascension from closing the Providence Health System hospital that served a low-income population [d63467621s3p0]. The D.C. city council passed an ordinance to give the city the power to block the hospital closing [d63467621s3p0]. The Attorney General ultimately withdrew the suit after reviewing plans for the hospital's closure [d63467621s3p0].
